headings: Certain businesses and assets of Prospect Medical Holdings, Inc. (collectively, "Prospect") (such acquisition, the "Prospect Acquisition")
Combination of Clinical, Administrative, and Technology Capabilities
Comprehensive and Effective Healthcare Management Programs
paragraphs: Astrana is a leading physician-centric, technology-powered, risk-bearing healthcare company. Leveraging its proprietary end-to-end technology solutions, Astrana operates an integrated healthcare delivery platform that enables providers to successfully participate in value-based care arrangements, thus empowering them to deliver accessible, high-quality care to patients in a cost-effective manner. We, together with our affiliated physician groups and consolidated subsidiaries and VIEs, provide coordinated outcome-based care, serving patients covered by private or public insurance provided through Medicare, Medicaid, and health maintenance organizations ("HMOs"), with a small portion of our revenue coming from non-insured patients. We provide care coordination services to each major constituent of the healthcare delivery system, including patients, families, primary care physicians, specialists, acute care hospitals, alternative sites of inpatient care, physician groups, and health plans. Our physician network consists of primary care physicians, specialist physicians, physician and specialist extenders, and hospitalists. Astrana's common stock is listed on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") and trades under the symbol "ASTH."

Led by a leadership team with several decades of experience, we have built a company and culture focused on physicians providing high-quality medical care, population health management, and patient care coordination. Through our integrated health network of more than 20,000 contracted physicians, we were responsible for coordinating value-based care for approximately 1.6 million patients as of December 31, 2025. As a result, we believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the shift in the U.S. healthcare industry toward value-based and results-oriented healthcare, with a focus on patient satisfaction, high-quality care, and cost efficiency. We implement and operate different innovative healthcare models, primarily including the following three reportable segments:

Our Care Partners segment is focused on building and managing high-quality and high-performance provider networks by partnering with, empowering, and investing in strong provider partners aligned on a shared vision for coordinated care delivery. Astrana meets providers where they are and enables independent providers to remain independent while succeeding in value-based care. Astrana acts as a "single payer" for our network of providers, enabling value-based care arrangements, including hospital shared-risk contracts. By leveraging our unique Care Enablement platform and ability to recruit, empower, and incentivize physicians to manage total cost of care effectively, we are able to organize partnered providers into successful multi-payer risk-bearing organizations that take on varying levels of risk, based on total cost of care across membership in all lines of business, including Medicare fee for service ("FFS"), Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, Commercial, and Exchange. These organizations make up our Care Partners segment, which consists of a network of risk-bearing organizations ("RBOs") that encompass independent practice associations ("IPAs"), accountable care organizations ("ACOs"), and state-specific entities such as Restricted Knox-Keene licensed health plans (sometimes referred to as "RKKs") in California. Through this network, our healthcare delivery entities are tasked with coordinating and providing high-quality care to patients within Astrana's ecosystem. This helps ensure seamless continuity of care among patients in different age groups, stages of life, and life circumstances.

An IPA is an association of independent physicians, or other organization that contracts with independent physicians. IPAs contract with HMOs, which are medical insurance groups that generally offer health care coverage to enrollees for a fixed annual fee, on a negotiated per capita rate, flat retainer fee, or negotiated FFS basis. Our affiliated IPAs comprise a network of independent providers, including primary care physicians, specialists, and other providers, who collectively care for patients. Our IPAs contract with various HMOs and other licensed healthcare service plans—such as Restricted Knox-Keene licensed health plans, as defined in the California Knox-Keene Health Care Service Plan Act of 1975, as amended (the "Knox-Keene Act"), to provide physician services to their enrollees, typically under capitated arrangements. Each HMO negotiates a fixed amount per member per month ("PMPM") that is to be paid to our IPAs. In return, the IPAs arrange for the delivery of healthcare services by contracting with physicians or professional medical corporations for primary care, specialty care, and other ancillary services. Our IPAs assume the financial risk of the cost of delivering certain healthcare services in excess of the fixed amounts received from health plans. Some of the risk is transferred to the contracted physicians or professional corporations and some is subject to stop-loss provisions in the contracts with the HMOs. With our owned RKKs in California, we can assume full financial responsibility, including both professional and institutional risk, for the medical costs of our members under the plans, which allows our Care Partners to manage a full spectrum of care.

An ACO is an organization that participates in one or more payment and delivery models sponsored by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services ("CMS") that provide high-quality and affordable care to Medicare FFS patients. The CMS programs allow provider groups to assume financial risk and potentially achieve a higher reward from participation in the respective program's attribution-based risk-sharing model. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company's ACOs participated in the ACO REACH Model and the Medicare Shared Savings Program ("MSSP").

Our Care Delivery segment is a patient-centric, data-driven organization focused on delivering high-quality and accessible care, serving approximately 1.6 million patients annually. As medical care has been increasingly delivered in clinic settings, many integrated health networks also operate healthcare facilities primarily focused on the diagnosis and/or care of outpatients, including those with chronic conditions such as heart disease and diabetes, to meet the primary healthcare needs of local communities. Our Care Delivery organization spans over 60 locations and includes:
• Primary care clinics, including post-acute care services and an acute care hospital facility;
• Specialty care clinics and inpatient services, including cardiac care, endocrinology, and ophthalmology, as well as hospitalist and intensivist services; and
• Ancillary service providers, such as urgent care centers, outpatient imaging centers, ambulatory surgery centers, full-service labs, and a specialty pharmacy.

We evaluate our Care Partners network based on specialty and geographic location, and then strategically engage in efforts to build or acquire practices and provider groups to address any gaps. This ensures that patients have access to high-quality care. Our ability to establish Care Delivery organizations tailored to specific markets enables us to scale effectively as we enter into new markets.

Our Care Enablement segment represents a comprehensive platform that integrates clinical, operational, financial, and administrative information, all powered by our proprietary technology suite. Our Care Enablement tools are leveraged across our Care Partners and Care Delivery lines of business as well as third-party providers outside of our Astrana ecosystem. Our Care Enablement segment provides solutions to payers and providers, including independent physicians, providers, and medical groups, as well as ACOs. The Company's platform meets providers and payers wherever they are on the spectrum of total cost of care, offering solutions for FFS entities and to providers open to taking upside and downside risks on professional and institutional spending, and across all patient types, including Medicare, Medicaid, Commercial, and Exchange-insured patients. This segment includes the Company's wholly owned subsidiaries that operate as management services organizations ("MSOs"),

to provide non-medical services under long-term management and/or administrative services agreements ("MSAs") with RBOs and other providers. By leveraging our Care Enablement platform, providers and payers can improve their ability to deliver high-quality care to their patients and achieve better patient, clinical, and financial outcomes.

Population health management ("PHM") seeks to improve health outcomes by monitoring and identifying individual patients, aggregating data, and providing a comprehensive clinical picture of each patient. PHM is a central trend within healthcare delivery, which includes the aggregation of patient data across multiple health information technology resources, the analysis of that data into a single, actionable patient record, and the actions through which care providers can improve both clinical and financial outcomes. When combined with effective care coordination, data-driven approaches can better connect patients to providers and resources, resulting in streamlined care delivery, improved clinical outcomes, and lower costs. A successful PHM platform requires a robust care and risk management infrastructure, a cohesive delivery system, and a well-managed partnership network.

headings: Risks Relating to the Prospect Acquisition.
Financing the Prospect Acquisition resulted in an increase in our indebtedness, which could adversely affect us, including by decreasing our business flexibility and increasing our interest expense.
Any difficulties integrating Prospect's operations could disrupt or have a material adverse effect on our current plans, business, or results of operations.

We could incur additional costs and expenses resulting from the July 7, 2025, bankruptcy of certain Prospect asset-seller entities and from the effect of the Prospect letter agreement dated July 1, 2025.
Risks Relating to Our General Business and Operations.
Our net operating loss carryforwards and certain other tax attributes will be subject to limitations.
The "One Big Beautiful Bill Act" could adversely affect our business and results of operations.
Uncertain or adverse economic conditions could adversely impact us.

We may be required to take write-downs or write-offs, restructuring, impairment, or other charges that could have a significant negative effect on our financial condition, results of operations, and stock price.

A prolonged disruption of or any actual or perceived difficulties in the capital and credit markets may adversely affect our future access to capital, our cost of capital, and our ability to continue operations.

If there is a change in accounting principles or the interpretation thereof affecting the consolidation of VIEs, it could impact our consolidation of total revenues derived from our affiliated physician groups.

We rely on complex software systems and hosted applications to operate our business, and our business may be disrupted if we are unable to successfully or efficiently update these systems or convert to new systems.
We may face risks associated with our use of certain AI and machine learning models.
If our internal control over financial reporting is not considered effective or material weaknesses are not remediated on a timely basis, our business and stock price could be adversely affected.
We currently derive a substantial portion of our revenues in California and are vulnerable to changes in that state.
Our success depends, to a significant degree, upon our ability to adapt to the ever-changing healthcare industry and the continued development of additional services.
Our reputation could be adversely impacted by sustainability and social policies and practices.
Risks Relating to Our Growth Strategy and Business Model.
Our growth strategy may not prove viable, and we may not realize expected results.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7, and our consolidated financial statements and related notes, before making a decision to invest in our common stock. Although the risks are organized by headings and each risk is discussed separately, many are interrelated. Disclosures of risks should not be interpreted to imply that the risks have not already materialized, and the risks and uncertainties described below may not be the only ones we face. If any of the risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, operating results, and prospects could be materially and adversely affected. In that event, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose part or all of your investment.
Our business is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties, discussed in more detail in the following section. These include, among others, the following key risks:

• We are subject to a variety of risks relating to the Prospect Acquisition, including a material increase in our indebtedness, challenges in integrating Prospect into our operations, and risks related to the acquired hospital.
• We may need to raise additional capital to grow, which might not be available.
• We could be negatively impacted by uncertain or adverse economic conditions and/or public health crises.
• Potential changes in laws, accounting principles, and regulations related to VIEs could impact our consolidation of total revenues derived from our affiliated physician groups.

paragraphs: The following management's discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto included in Part II, Item 8, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

In this section, "we," "our," "ours," and "us" refer to Astrana Health, Inc. ("Astrana") and its consolidated subsidiaries and affiliated entities, as appropriate, including its consolidated variable interest entities ("VIEs").

Astrana Health, Inc. is a leading physician-centric, technology-powered, risk-bearing healthcare management company. Leveraging its proprietary population health management and healthcare delivery platform, Astrana operates an integrated, value-based healthcare model, that aims to empower the providers in its network to deliver the highest quality of care to its patients in a cost-effective manner. Together with our affiliated physician groups and consolidated entities, we cost-effectively provide coordinated outcomes-based medical care.

Through our risk-bearing organizations ("RBOs") with more than 20,000 contracted physicians, we were responsible for coordinating the care for approximately 1.6 million patients, primarily in California, as of December 31, 2025. These covered patients are managed care members whose health coverage is provided either through their employers, directly from a health plan, or as a result of their eligibility for Medicaid or Medicare benefits. Our managed patients benefit from an integrated approach that places physicians at the center of patient care and utilizes sophisticated risk management techniques and clinical protocols to deliver high-quality, cost-effective care.

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (the "OBBBA"), signed on July 4, 2025, introduces Medicaid work-requirement pilots and tighter provider tax rules beginning in 2026. We expect to see tax impacts from the following changes, including the restoration of 100% bonus depreciation, allowing the current year deduction of research and development expenses, and changing the 163j interest limitation from earnings before tax to EBITDA. We anticipate the OBBBA will not have a material impact on tax expense and did not identify a material impact in 2025. While we are still evaluating the full downstream effects, we believe Astrana is well-positioned to navigate these changes and view these headwinds as manageable. Our diversified footprint, strong track record of Medicaid performance, and investment in care-enablement infrastructure provide meaningful insulation. We remain focused on maintaining continuity of care and supporting our state partners through this policy transition.

On January 26, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services ("CMS") issued an advance notice detailing proposed 2027 Medicare Advantage payment rates (the "2027 Advance Notice"). CMS accepted comments on the 2027 Advance Notice until February 25, 2026 and intends to publish the final 2027 rate announcement no later than April 6, 2026. If the proposed rates are finalized, we anticipate impact to the Medicare line of business. We expect the impact of the proposed risk adjustment model changes to be materially less significant for Astrana than for the broader Medicare Advantage market. While we are still evaluating the full downstream effects, we believe Astrana is well-positioned to navigate these changes and view these headwinds as manageable.
Certain businesses and assets of Prospect Medical Holdings, Inc. (collectively, "Prospect") (such acquisition, the "Prospect Acquisition")

On July 1, 2025, we completed our previously announced acquisition of Prospect, including its California-licensed health plan (Prospect Health Plan), its medical groups in multiple states (Prospect Medical Groups), its management service organization (Prospect Medical Systems), its pharmacy (RightRx), and Foothill Regional Medical Center ("FRMC"). Prospect is a physician-centric, risk-bearing healthcare company that operates an integrated healthcare delivery platform, enabling a network of over 11,000 providers to participate in value-based care arrangements, and empowering them to deliver accessible, high-quality care to patients in a cost-effective manner. Prospect enables physicians to deliver payer-agnostic, patient-centered care across Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and Commercial lines of business. The acquisition significantly expanded our provider network and enhanced our ability to offer increased access, quality, and value to our members (see Note 3 — "Business Combinations and Goodwill" to our consolidated financial statements under Item 8 in this Annual Report on Form 10-K).

On February 26, 2025, we amended and restated our credit agreement with Truist Bank, in its capacities as administrative agent for the lenders (the "Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement"). The Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement provides for (a) a five-year revolving credit facility ("Revolver Loan") to us of $300.0 million, which includes a letter of credit sub-facility of up to $100.0 million and a swingline loan sub-facility of $25.0 million, (b) a five-year term loan A credit facility ("Term Loan") to us of $250.0 million, and (c) a five-year delayed draw term loan credit facility ("DDTL A" and, together with the Term Loan, the "Term Loans") to us of $745.0 million of which $707.3 million was drawn to fund the Prospect Acquisition. The Term Loan and Revolver Loan were used to, among other things, refinance certain existing indebtedness of ours and certain subsidiaries, pay transaction costs and expenses arising in connection with the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, and provide for working capital needs and other general corporate purposes. The DDTL A was used to fund the Prospect Acquisition, and, in addition to the foregoing, the Revolver Loan was used to finance certain future permitted acquisitions and permitted investments and capital expenditures (see Note 10 — "Credit Facility and Bank Loans" to our consolidated financial statements under Item 8 in this Annual Report on Form 10-K).

We partnered with a provider group in Southern California and with Intermountain Health across southern Nevada with the collaboration goal to expand access to coordinated, high-quality care, enhance primary care access, improve patient outcomes, and advance the healthcare infrastructure through shared technology and care management programs.

Our revenue, which is recorded in the period during which services are rendered and earned, generally on a monthly basis, primarily consists of capitation revenue, risk pool settlements and incentives, management fee income, fee-for-services ("FFS") revenue, and other revenue primarily consisting of revenues earned from maternity care and Hospital Quality Assurance Fee Program ("HQAF"). The form of billing and related collection risk for such services may vary by revenue type and customer.

Our largest expenses consist of the cost of: (i) patient care paid to contracted providers; (ii) information technology equipment and software; and (iii) hiring staff to provide management and administrative support services to our affiliated physician groups, as further described in the following sections. These services include claims processing, utilization management, contracting, accounting, credentialing, and administrative oversight.

Our Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are supplemental performance measures of our operations for financial and operational decision-making, and are used as a supplemental means of evaluating period-to-period comparisons on a consistent basis. Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as earnings before interest expense, interest income, income taxes, depreciation, and amortization, excluding income or loss from equity method investments, non-recurring and non-cash transactions, and stock-based compensation. We define Adjusted EBITDA margin as Adjusted EBITDA over total revenue.

Our adjusted EPS - diluted is a supplemental performance measure of our operations for financial and operational decision-making and is used as a supplemental means of evaluating period-to-period comparisons on a consistent basis. We define adjusted EPS - diluted as adjusted net income attributable to Astrana over weighted average shares of common stock outstanding - diluted. Adjusted net income attributable to Astrana is calculated as net income, excluding income or loss from equity method investments, non-recurring and non-cash transactions, stock-based compensation, amortization of intangibles, certain tax adjustments, and amounts related to non-controlling interest.

paragraphs: Astrana 是一家以醫師為中心、以科技為驅動、承擔風險的醫療保健公司。透過其專屬的端到端科技解決方案，Astrana 運作一個整合的醫療照護平台，使提供者能夠成功參與以價值為基礎的照護安排，從而賦予他們以成本效益的方式為患者提供可近用且高品質的照護。我們與我們的附屬醫師羣體及合併子公司與VIEs共同提供協調的結果導向照護，服務使用私人或公共保險的患者，這些保險由Medicare、Medicaid及健康維護組織（"HMOs"）提供，一小部分的收入來自非保險患者。我們為醫療照護系統的每個主要參與者提供照護協調服務，包括患者、家庭、門診醫師、專科醫師、急性照護醫院、替代性住院照護場所、醫師羣體及健康計畫。我們的醫師網路包括門診醫師、專科醫師、醫師及專科延伸人員以及醫院內科醫師。Astrana 的普通股在 Nasdaq 股票市場 LLC（"Nasdaq"）上市，交易代碼為 "ASTH."

由具數十年經驗的領導團隊所領導，我們建立了一家專注於醫師提供高品質醫療照護、人口健康管理及患者照護協調的公司與文化。透過我們超過20,000名簽約醫師的整合健康網路，我們截至2025年12月31日為約160萬名患者協調以價值為基礎的照護。因此，我們相信我們處於美國醫療保健產業向以價值為基礎及結果導向醫療照護轉變的優勢位置，著重於患者滿意度、高品質照護及成本效益。我們實踐並運作不同的創新醫療模式，主要包括以下三個應報告分部：

我們的照護夥伴分部專注於建立並管理高品質且高績效的提供者網路，透過與、賦能及投資於與協調照護交付有共同願景的強大提供者夥伴。Astrana 在提供者所在之處與他們接觸，使獨立提供者能保持獨立性同時在以價值為基礎的照護中成功。Astrana 當作我們提供者網路的 "單一付款人"，使我們能進行以價值為基礎的照護安排，包括醫院共擔風險契約。透過我們獨特的照護啟動平台及招募、賦能及激勵醫師有效管理總照護成本的能力，我們能將合作的提供者組織成成功的多付款人風險承擔組織，根據總照護成本在所有業務線中的會員情況，承擔不同層級的風險，包括Medicare費用服務（"FFS"）、Medicare Advantage、Medicaid、商業及交易所。這些組織組成我們的照護夥伴分部，該分部包括一個風險承擔組織（"RBOs"）網路，涵蓋獨立實踐協會（"IPAs"）、責任照護組織（"ACOs"）以及加州特定的實體，如 Restricted Knox-Keene 註冊健康計畫（有時稱為 "RKKs"）。透過這個網路，我們的醫療照護實體被賦予協調並為患者在Astrana生態系內提供高品質照護的任務。這有助於確保不同年齡層、生命階段及生活情況的患者之間的照護連續性。

IPAs 是一個由獨立醫師或其他組織組成的協會，與獨立醫師簽約。IPAs 與 HMOs 簽約，HMOs 是醫療保險集團，通常以固定年度費用、每 capita 率、固定保留費或協議 FFS 基礎為 enrollees 提供醫療照護覆蓋。我們的附屬 IPAs 組成一個獨立提供者的網路，包括門診醫師、專科醫師及其他提供者，他們共同為患者提供照護。我們的 IPAs 與各種 HMOs 及其他經許可的醫療服務計畫簽約，如 Restricted Knox-Keene 註冊健康計畫，如加州 Knox-Keene 健康照護服務計畫法於1975年制定（"Knox-Keene Act"）所定義，以為其 enrollees 提供醫師服務，通常在封頂安排下進行。每個 HMO 與我們的 IPAs 簽訂固定每月每位 enrollee（"PMPM"）的金額，作為支付。作為回報，IPAs 透過與醫師或專業醫療公司簽約，為門診、專科及其他輔助服務提供醫療服務。我們的 IPAs 承擔因醫療服務成本超過健康計畫支付的固定金額而產生的財務風險。部分風險轉移給簽約的醫師或專業公司，部分則根據與 HMOs 的契約中的停止損失條款。透過我們在加州擁有 RKKs，我們可以承擔會員在計畫下的全部醫療費用，包括專業及機構風險，這使我們的照護夥伴能管理完整的照護範疇。
ACO 是參與由美國醫療保險與醫療援助中心（"CMS"）贊助的一或多種付款及交付模式的組織，為 Medicare FFS 患者提供高品質且負擔得起的照護。CMS 程式允許提供者羣體承擔財務風險，並可能從參與相應程式之歸屬風險共擔模式中獲得更高回報。截至2025年12月31日，本公司之 ACOs 參與 ACO REACH 模式及 Medicare 共享節省計畫（"MSSP"）。
我們的照護交付分部是一家以患者為中心、數據驅動的組織，專注於提供高品質且可近用的照護，每年服務約160萬名患者。隨著醫療照護越來越在診所環境中進行，許多整合健康網路也運作主要專注於診斷及/或照護 outpatient 的醫療設施，包括患有慢性病如心臟病及糖尿病的患者，以滿足當地社區的基礎醫療需求。我們的照護交付組織涵蓋超過60個據點，包括：
• 門診診所，包括後續照護服務及急性照護醫院設施；
• 專科診所及住院服務，包括心臟科、內分泌科及眼科，以及醫院內科及重症監護服務；
• 補充性服務提供者，例如急診中心、門診影像中心、日間手術中心、完整服務實驗室，以及專門藥房。
我們根據專門領域及地理位置評估 Care Partners 網路，並戰略性地投入努力以建立或收購實踐及服務提供者羣組，以解決任何缺口。這確保患者能獲得高品質的照護。我們能建立符合特定市場需求的 Care Delivery 組織，使我們在進入新市場時能有效擴張。

我們的 Care Enablement 分部代表一個整合臨牀、運營、財務及行政資訊的綜合平台，所有資訊皆由我們的專有技術組合驅動。我們的 Care Enablement 工具被應用於 Care Partners 及 Care Delivery 事業線，以及 Astrana 生態系統以外的第三方提供者。Care Enablement 分部為支付者及服務提供者（包括獨立醫生、服務提供者及醫療團體）以及 ACOs 提供解決方案。本公司的平台可適應支付者及服務提供者在總醫療成本光譜中的任何位置，提供 FFS 機構的解決方案，以及對願意承擔專業及機構開支風險的服務提供者，並涵蓋所有患者類型，包括 Medicare、Medicaid、商業保險及交易所保險患者。此分部包含本公司全資子公司，這些子公司運作為管理服務機構（"MSOs"）
以在長期管理及/或行政服務協議（"MSAs"）下為 RBOs 及其他服務提供者提供非醫療服務。透過運用我們的 Care Enablement 平台，服務提供者及支付者可提升其為患者提供高品質照護的能力，並實現更好的患者、臨牀及財務成果。

人口健康管理（"PHM"）旨在透過監測及識別個別患者、彙整數據，並提供每位患者的完整臨牀畫像，來改善健康結果。PHM 是醫療照護交付中的核心趨勢，包括跨多個健康資訊科技資源彙整患者數據、將該數據分析為單一可操作的患者記錄，以及透過這些行動改善臨牀及財務結果。當與有效的照護協調結合時，數據驅動的方法能更有效地將患者與服務提供者及資源連結，實現流暢的照護交付、改善臨牀結果及降低成本。成功的 PHM 平台需要強大的照護及風險管理基礎設施、協調的交付系統，以及良好管理的夥伴關係網路。
根據已建立的 MSAs，我們的 MSOs 有權處理與持續業務運作相關的各種非醫療決策，並提供服務，包括但不限於：

paragraphs: 下列管理層討論與分析應配合審計後之合併財務報表及附註，包含於本年度報告表 10-K 第二部分，第 8 項 "財務報表與補充資料" 中。
本節中，"我們"、"我們的"、"我們的"及"我們"指 Astrana Health, Inc. ("Astrana") 及其合併子公司與附屬機構，如適用，包括其合併之可變利益實體 ("VIEs")。
Astrana Health, Inc. 是一家以醫師為中心、以科技為動力、承擔風險的醫療管理公司。透過其專屬之人口健康管理與醫療服務平台，Astrana 運作一整體價值導向之醫療模式，旨在協助其網路內之醫療提供者以成本效益方式提供最高品質之照護。與我們之附屬醫師羣及合併機構合作，我們以成本效益方式提供協調之結果導向醫療服務。

透過我們承擔風險之組織 ("RBOs")，擁有超過 20,000 名簽約醫師，我們為約 1.6 百萬名患者協調照護，主要位於加州，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。這些被覆蓋之患者為管理照護會員，其健康保險由僱主提供、直接來自健康保險計畫，或因符合 Medicaid 或 Medicare 福利資格而獲得。我們之管理患者受益於整體化之方法，將醫師置於患者照護中心，並運用先進之風險管理技術與臨牀協議，以提供高品質、成本效益之照護。

一項大美觀法案 ("OBBBA") 於 2025 年 7 月 4 日簽署，於 2026 年開始引入 Medicaid 工作要求試點與更嚴格之供應商稅務規則。我們預期會因以下變動產生稅務影響，包括恢復 100% 優化折舊、允許當年度扣除研究與發展費用，以及將 163j 利息限制從稅前盈餘變更為 EBITDA。我們預期 OBBBA 對稅務費用不會有重大影響，且在 2025 年未發現重大影響。雖然我們仍在評估完整的下游影響，我們認為 Astrana 有良好定位來應對這些變動，並視這些挑戰為可管理。我們多元化的業務版圖、強大的 Medicaid 表現紀錄，以及對照護基礎設施的投資提供了重要的保護。

2026 年 1 月 26 日，美國醫療保險與醫療服務管理局 ("CMS") 發布一份預告通知，說明 2027 年 Medicare Advantage 支付率 ("2027 預告通知")。CMS 接受對 2027 預告通知之意見至 2026 年 2 月 25 日，並預計於 2026 年 4 月 6 日前發布最終 2027 年率公告。若建議之支付率確定，我們預期會對 Medicare 事業線產生影響。我們預期建議之風險調整模型變動對 Astrana 的影響將比對廣泛 Medicare Advantage 市場為之顯著較小。雖然我們仍在評估完整的下游影響，我們認為 Astrana 有良好定位來應對這些變動，並視這些挑戰為可管理。
Prospect Medical Holdings, Inc. 某些業務與資產 (合稱 "Prospect") (此項收購，稱為 "Prospect 收購")

我們於 2025 年 7 月 1 日完成先前公告之 Prospect 收購，包括其在加州執照之健康保險計畫 (Prospect Health Plan)、其在多州之醫療羣 (Prospect Medical Groups)、其管理服務機構 (Prospect Medical Systems)、其藥房 (RightRx)，以及 Foothill 區域醫療中心 ("FRMC")。Prospect 是一家以醫師為中心、承擔風險之醫療公司，運作一整體醫療服務平台，使超過 11,000 名醫療提供者參與價值導向之照護安排，並協助他們以成本效益方式提供可近取、高品質之照護給患者。Prospect 使醫師能提供與支付者無關、以患者為中心之照護，涵蓋 Medicare Advantage、Medicaid 及商業業務線。此項收購大幅擴充我們之醫療提供者網路，並增強我們提供更高可近取性、品質與價值給會員之能力 (請參閱我們合併財務報表之附註 3 — "企業合併與商譽"，包含於本年度報告表 10-K 第二部分，第 8 項 "財務報表與補充資料" 中。)

於 2025 年 2 月 26 日，我們與 Truist Bank 簽訂信用協議，Truist Bank 作為貸款人之行政代理（"第二修正重述信用協議"）。第二修正重述信用協議提供（a）五年期循環信用貸款（"循環貸款"）給我們 300.0 百萬美元，包含信用證子貸款上限 100.0 百萬美元及 swingline 貸款子貸款 25.0 百萬美元，（b）五年期 A 期貸款信用貸款（"期貸款"）給我們 250.0 百萬美元，以及（c）五年期延後提款期貸款信用貸款（"延後提款期貸款 A" 以及與期貸款合稱 "期貸款"）給我們 745.0 百萬美元，其中 707.3 百萬美元已提款用以資助 Prospect 收購。期貸款與循環貸款已用於，除其他事項外，重組我們及我們之子公司之現有債務，支付與第二修正重述信用協議相關之交易成本及費用，並提供營運資金需求及其他一般企業用途。延後提款期貸款 A 已用於資助 Prospect 收購，此外，循環貸款亦用於資金融通未來允許之收購及投資及資本支出（請參閱我們合併財務報表之附註 10 — "信用貸款及銀行貸款"，於本年度報告 10-K 表單之第 8 項項目下）。
我們與南加州之服務供應商羣組及南內華達之 Intermountain Health 合作，目標為擴大協調且高品質照護之存取，提升門診照護存取，改善病患結果，並透過共享科技及照護管理計畫推進醫療基礎建設。
我們之營業收入，係於服務提供及賺取期間記錄，通常為每月為單位，主要由資本化收入、風險池結算及激勵金、管理費用收入、費用服務收入（"費用服務收入"）及其它收入，主要為來自產婦照護及醫院品質保證費用計畫（"醫院品質保證費用計畫"）之收入組成。此類服務之開票方式及相關收款風險可能因收入類型及客戶而異。
我們最大之費用為：（i）支付給合約供應商之病人照護費用；（ii）資訊科技設備及軟體；以及（iii）聘僱員工以提供管理及行政支援服務給我們之合作醫生羣組，如後文所述。這些服務包括申報處理、使用率管理、合約、會計、認證及行政監督。

我們之調整後營業現金流（Adjusted EBITDA）及調整後營業現金流邊際（Adjusted EBITDA margin）為我們營運之補充性績效指標，用於財務及營運決策，並作為評估期間對期間比較之補充性方法。調整後營業現金流計算為營業利益扣除利息支出、利息收入、所得稅、折舊及攤銷，排除來自權益法投資之收益或虧損、非反覆及非現金交易，以及股票基於報酬。我們定義調整後營業現金流邊際為調整後營業現金流除以總營業收入。
我們之調整後每股盈餘（稀釋後）為我們營運之補充性績效指標，用於財務及營運決策，並作為評估期間對期間比較之補充性方法。我們定義調整後每股盈餘（稀釋後）為調整後歸屬於 Astrana 之淨收入除以稀釋後之普通股權益平均數。調整後歸屬於 Astrana 之淨收入計算為淨收入，排除來自權益法投資之收益或虧損、非反覆及非現金交易、股票基於報酬、無形資產攤銷、某些稅務調整，以及與非控制權益相關之金額。

headings: 與前景收購相關的風險。
籌措前景收購資金導致我們的負債增加，這可能會對我們產生不利影響，包括降低我們的業務彈性並增加我們的利息支出。
任何整合前景運營的困難都可能幹擾或對我們目前的計畫、業務或營運結果產生重大不利影響。
我們可能因2025年7月7日某些前景資產賣方實體破產，以及2025年7月1日前景書面協議的影響而產生額外的成本和費用。
與我們一般業務及運營相關的風險。
我們的淨營業虧損結轉及某些其他稅務屬性將受到限制。
「一張大美麗帳單法案」可能對我們的業務及營運結果產生不利影響。
不確定或惡劣的經濟條件可能對我們造成不利影響。
我們可能需要進行減記、減損、重整、減損或其它費用，這些費用可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果及股票價格產生顯著的負面影響。
資本與信貸市場若出現長期中斷或任何實際或被認為的困難，可能對我們未來取得資本的能力、資本成本以及持續營運的能力產生不利影響。
若會計準則或其解釋方式發生變更，影響VIEs的合併，可能會影響我們來自附屬醫生集團的總收入合併。
我們依賴複雜的軟體系統與寄託應用程式來運作業務，若我們無法成功或高效地更新這些系統或轉換至新系統，業務可能會受到幹擾。
我們可能面臨與使用某些人工智能及機器學習模型相關的風險。
若我們的財務報告內部控製被認為不具備有效性或重大缺陷未及時修正，業務及股票價格可能會受到不利影響。
我們目前在加州取得相當大一部分的收入，並對該州的變動相當敏感。
本公司之成功在很大程度上取決於我們適應不斷變化的醫療產業及持續發展附加服務之能力。
本公司聲譽可能因永續性及社會政策與實踐而受到負面影響。
與本公司成長策略及商業模式相關之風險。
本公司成長策略可能無法實現，且我們可能無法實現預期之結果。
paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告表10-K中所有其他資訊，包括第二部分第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」以及我們的合併財務報表與相關附註，再做是否投資本公司普通股之決定。雖然風險已依標題分類，並分別討論，但許多風險是相互關聯的。風險揭露不應被解讀為表示這些風險尚未發生，且下列所描述的風險與不確定性可能並非我們唯一面臨的風險。若任何風險實際發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與前景造成重大且不利的影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。
我們的業務面臨許多風險與不確定性，詳情請參閱後述之相關段落。這些風險包括但不限於以下關鍵風險：
• 我們面臨與Prospect收購相關的多種風險，包括本公司負債大幅增加、整合Prospect至我們營運之挑戰，以及與所收購醫院相關的風險。
• 我們可能需要籌措額外資金以促進成長，但此資金可能無法取得。
• 我們可能因不確定或惡劣的總體經濟條件與/或公共衛生危機而受到負面影響。
• 與VIEs相關之法律、會計準則與規範潛在變更，可能影響我們對來自我們附屬醫師羣體之總營收之合併。
